answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust flow like a river that widens only with time: every new identity starts in a narrow channel with tiny transaction limits, and its cap grows only after weeks of verified honest work. Before dawn of each settlement, peers audit the work history, and a single fraud finding drains the agent's vault of earned reputation back to zero. Creating thousands of fake identities is therefore useless: each must slowly earn its own standing, and the attacker pays months of real work for every sock puppet while honest agents keep compounding trust.
